clue.text: Dutch will mind sailing to work

definitions.text: Dutch will mind sailing to work

indicators.note: sailing suggests things moving about freely, so the letters of the two words are set in motion and rearranged

explanation.surface: A Dutchman agrees to sail off to his job.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sailing' signals the anagram of WILL MIND; the whole clue then describes the answer, a Dutch machine that needs its sails turning to work.
explanation.definitionFit: Dutch mills grind grain or pump water only when their sails turn in the breeze.

clue.text: The power of women's crew

parts.note: W is the abbreviation for women
an eight is a rowing crew

explanation.surface: A women's rowing team shows its strength.
explanation.definitionFit: Weight means influence or force, as in the weight of an argument.

clue.text: Lump of game served up in New England

indicators.note: the game sits inside the New England abbreviation
in a down clue served up means turned upward, so the game is read bottom to top

parts.note: ludo is a board game

explanation.surface: A bit of venison is on the menu in Massachusetts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lump of game' suggests a chunk of venison; 'served up' turns LUDO upward to read ODUL in this down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: A nodule is a small rounded swelling or knob.

clue.text: Snake -vicious, with brightly coloured back

parts.note: mean means nasty or vicious

indicators.note: back signals that the colour word is read backwards

parts.note: red is a bright colour

explanation.surface: A nasty serpent with a vivid red back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Snake' is a verb here, to wind about; 'back' reverses RED to DER.
explanation.definitionFit: A river that winds about follows a twisting, looping course.

clue.text: Pencil in the clue? To the contrary!

definitions.text: Pencil in the clue? To the contrary!

parts.words: Pencil in the clue? To the contrary!
parts.note: the word pencil sits in the clue; reverse that and the answer is the thing that sits in a pencil

explanation.walkthrough: The joke reverses the old phrase about what is in a pencil: not a pencil in the clue, but the clue's answer in the pencil.
explanation.definitionFit: Pencil cores are graphite, traditionally called by the name of a heavy metal.

clue.text: Ward for when one has an attack

explanation.surface: A hospital ward is needed for someone who has suffered a heart attack.
explanation.definitionFit: A ward is a person in your care or keeping; an attack, as by cavalry, is a rush at the enemy.

clue.text: Hold-up in the locks?

parts.note: reads like a delay at canal locks, but means something that holds hair up

explanation.definitionFit: A U-shaped pin keeps the hair pinned in place.

clue.text: Had your job taken over-and all your worries too?

definitions.text: Had your job taken over-and all your worries too?

parts.words: Had your job taken over-and all your worries too?
parts.note: a worker whose shift is taken over by a replacement is also freed of cares, two senses of one word

explanation.definitionFit: A sentry is replaced by the next guard, and an anxious person feels great ease once worry lifts.

clue.text: Showing up for late sitting

parts.note: ex means former, as late does
posing is sitting for a portrait

explanation.surface: Arriving for an evening session.
explanation.walkthrough: 'late sitting' looks like a meeting in the evening, but 'late' means former.
explanation.definitionFit: Exposing someone is revealing their wrongdoing to the world.

clue.text: Ship carrying person from the sub-continent

parts.note: the Indian sub-continent, named here by its main country
a man is a person

explanation.surface: A vessel has an Indian passenger aboard.
explanation.walkthrough: 'person from the sub-continent' reads as one Indian passenger, but the clue splits into two pieces, the country first.
explanation.definitionFit: East Indiamen were large merchant vessels trading with India in the days of sail.

clue.text: Stimulus given to a sound lad

indicators.note: the clue asks for something that sounds like a lad, so a boy's name is said aloud

parts.note: Philip is a lad's name, given here as an example

explanation.surface: Encouragement is offered to a healthy boy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sound' looks like an adjective meaning healthy, but it signals a word heard aloud: the boy's name PHILIP.
explanation.definitionFit: A fillip is a boost or spur that livens something up.

clue.text: A Gallic cook hostile In manner

indicators.note: to cook figures is to fiddle with them, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A French chef is unfriendly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cook' looks like a noun for the Frenchman, but it is a verb signalling the anagram.
explanation.definitionFit: An icy, frosty manner is cold and unfriendly.

clue.text: The chap's holding a cover to the chemical

indicators.note: one piece holds another within it, so it goes round the rest

parts.note: he is a pronoun for a chap
a lid is a cover

explanation.surface: A man keeps a lid on the chemical.
explanation.definitionFit: A halide is a compound of a halogen such as chlorine with another element, a class of chemical.

clue.text: Ships' barbers?

explanation.surface: Naval hairdressers.
explanation.definitionFit: Clippers were fast sailing vessels; barbers trim hair, so they are people who clip.

clue.text: Composer in party upset — went too far

indicators.note: the composer goes inside the party
upset in a down clue turns the party word upside down

parts.note: a do is a party
Verdi was an Italian opera composer

explanation.surface: A musician at a celebration becomes distressed and overreaches.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' turns DO upward to read OD in this down clue, and the Italian opera composer sits inside.
explanation.definitionFit: To overdo something is to take it to excess.

clue.text: Undertaking business that may be a cause of extreme disquiet

explanation.surface: A funeral firm may give rise to deep worry.
explanation.definitionFit: An undertaker's firm deals in burials, so it is jokingly a business of the grave; a serious worry is great alarm.

clue.text: Drink from the basin

indicators.note: the drink is made from the letters of the words that follow

explanation.surface: Taking a drink out of the washbasin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'from' signals that THE BASIN is the raw material, rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Absinthe is a strong green aniseed spirit.

clue.text: Not the promoter's right-hand man

parts.note: reads as an aide not trusted by an organiser, but means a boxer on a fight promoter's bill who leads with the left

explanation.definitionFit: A left-handed boxer, as opposed to an orthodox right-handed one.

clue.text: A lobster pate substitute?

indicators.note: a substitute stands in for the original, so these letters are replaced by a rearrangement of themselves

explanation.surface: Something to spread instead of lobster pâté.
explanation.walkthrough: 'substitute' signals the anagram of A LOBSTER PATE, and the result is indeed a cheaper fish spread that might stand in for it.
explanation.definitionFit: A cheap smoked-herring spread for toast is the kind of thing served when lobster is too dear.

clue.text: The guiding-line in that place

parts.note: a rein is a strap for guiding a horse

explanation.surface: The guide rope is located there.
explanation.definitionFit: Therein is a formal word meaning within or in that thing.

clue.text: Defeat, since no truce is engineered

indicators.note: something engineered is built or contrived, so the letters are reworked

explanation.surface: A loss follows since no ceasefire is arranged.
explanation.definitionFit: To trounce is to beat heavily.

clue.text: Weapon needed for military force on landing stage

parts.note: RA is the Royal Artillery, a British army force
a pier is a landing stage

explanation.surface: Arms are needed for troops landing at a jetty.
explanation.definitionFit: A rapier is a slender thrusting sword.

clue.text: Bird, decapitating this dog

parts.note: take the head off the dog's name and a bird of prey is left

explanation.walkthrough: The clue works backwards: removing the first letter of the hound gives a bird of prey, so the solver must find a dog whose name contains a bird.
explanation.definitionFit: A small hunting hound with long ears, bred for chasing hares.

clue.text: Undaunted, I printed amendment

indicators.note: an amendment alters the word printed, rearranging its letters

explanation.surface: Correcting what one has put in print takes courage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'amendment' rearranges PRINTED into NTREPID, which follows the I.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone intrepid is fearless and not put off by danger.

clue.text: Very good fabric -that's a comfort

parts.note: so means very, as in so kind
lace is a fine and costly fabric

explanation.surface: Fine material is a source of comfort.
explanation.definitionFit: Solace is consolation in distress.

clue.text: Ice in the drink

parts.note: reads like a cube in a glass, but the drink is slang for the sea

explanation.definitionFit: A floating sheet of sea ice.

clue.text: Two pages in a row, expecting something of him?

indicators.note: the two pages go inside the row

parts.note: a tier is a row, as of seats
p is the abbreviation for page, so two pages are pp

explanation.surface: Two hotel pageboys stand in line waiting for a guest's gratuity.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is a description: the waiter or porter expects a gratuity from the generous guest.
explanation.definitionFit: A person who leaves gratuities is the one staff hope will hand over money.

clue.text: Monarch of the glen, rattling his chains

indicators.note: monarch of the glen puts the clan word before the king word

parts.note: a glen is a Scottish valley, home of a Highland clan
a king is a monarch

explanation.surface: The Highland stag, the 'Monarch of the Glen' painting, is imagined as a chained ghost.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The Monarch of the Glen' is a famous Victorian painting of a Highland stag by Landseer; 'of' puts the clan before the king.
explanation.definitionFit: A ghost rattling its chains makes a metallic clashing noise.

clue.text: Girl entering West Indies given another name

indicators.note: the West Indies abbreviation goes into the other name

parts.note: Edna is another girl's name

explanation.surface: A woman who moves to the Caribbean takes a new name.
explanation.definitionFit: Edwina is a woman's first name.

clue.text: Run over by military vehicle

parts.note: RE, the Royal Engineers, is a military corps
a hearse is a vehicle for a coffin

explanation.surface: Someone is knocked down by an army truck.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Run over' looks like a road accident; it means go through again. The Royal Engineers are a British Army corps.
explanation.definitionFit: To practise a play or speech is to go through it beforehand.
